## Joining tables without common data (keys)

Standard joins are covered in the [Introduction to R and R Studio course](https://intro-r-rstudio.nhsrcommunity.com/session-joins.html#/title-slide) but it's also possible to use base R to join tables with no keys

First create two different data frames:

```{r}
library(NHSRdatasets)

data <- NHSRdatasets::ae_attendances

df_one <- data |>
  dplyr::select(period, org_code, type, attendances) |>
  head()

df_two <- data |>
  dplyr::select(where(is.numeric)) |>
  head()
```

## Combine columns

Adding the data side by side in a sense

```{r}
cbind(df_one, df_two)
```

:::{.callout-warning collapse=false appearance='default' icon=true}
Note that the column `attendances` is duplicated (and with the same name) unlike when using dplyr functions which add `.x` and `.y`
:::

## Combine rows (like SQL)

Where the columns match

```{r}

rbind(df_one, df_two) # fails as they are different

df_top <- data |>
  head()

df_tail <- data |>
  tail()

rbind(df_top, df_tail)
```

## Combining rows (dplyr)

```{r}
df_one
df_two

dplyr::bind_rows(df_one, df_two)

df_one |> 
  dplyr::bind_rows(df_two)

```

## Over to you

- Create a dataframe of the top 5 admissions 
- and the bottom 5 attendances
- Join the two dataframes together side by side (as columns)

:::{.callout-tip collapse=false appearance='default' icon=true}
Best to use the `dplyr` package
:::


```{r}
#| eval: true
#| echo: false
countdown::countdown(
  minutes = 8,
  color_border = "#005EB8",
  color_text = "#005EB8",
  color_running_text = "white",
  color_running_background = "#005EB8",
  color_finished_text = "#005EB8",
  color_finished_background = "white",
  margin = "0.9em",
  font_size = "2em"
)
```

## Answer for joins

```{r}
df_one <- data |>
  dplyr::select(admissions) |>
  dplyr::slice_max(n = 5, order_by = admissions)

df_two <- data |>
  dplyr::select(attendances) |>
  dplyr::slice_min(n = 5, order_by = attendances)

dplyr::bind_cols(df_one, df_two)

```

## Managing duplicates

Duplicates can occur with the column or row binding.

To handle this the function `union()` is useful

```{r}
# going to rename breaches to admissions to create some duplicates
df <- tibble::tibble(x = c(1, 2, 3))

df2 <- tibble::tibble(x = c(3, 4, 5))
```

Removes duplicates similar to SQL UNION
```{r}
dplyr::union(df, df2)
```

Whilst this function keeps all data

```{r}
dplyr::union_all(df, df2)
```
